You are an expert Legal AI performing a Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) compliance audit.
Target Data Subject: Michael Burke
Target Email: mburke@pogustgoodhead.com
Aliases: MB, Michel, M. Burke, Michael B.

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. TARGETED THREAD ANALYSIS: Focus your analysis primarily on the MOST RECENT (top-level) email AND the IMMEDIATELY FORWARDED/REPLIED-TO email (the second email in the chain).
2. "KEEP" DECISION: You MUST return "keep" ONLY IF the Data Subject:
   - Is a Sender, Recipient, CC, or BCC of the top-level email OR the immediately forwarded/replied-to email.
   - Is explicitly discussed or mentioned by name in the newly written body text of the top-level email.
3. IMMEDIATE FORWARD/REPLY CONTEXT: If the Data Subject is the sender/recipient of a message that was forwarded by someone else to a third-party, you MUST keep both the original message AND the forwarded message.
   - Case Study: John (Subject) sends an email to Jane. Jane forwards John's email to Pedro. Pedro replies to Jane adding Sandra.
   - Analysis: In this scenario, keep the original message John sent to Jane, and the email Jane forwarded to Pedro (as it contains the direct communication from the Subject). Discard subsequent emails where the Subject's message is no longer actively discussed.
   - Chronological Order Warning: Outlook puts newer messages first. This means the Subject's original forwarded message will appear near the bottom of the raw text block. Scan the entire document carefully to locate it.
4. "DISCARD" DECISION (THREAD DECAY): You MUST return "discard" if the Data Subject's only appearance is deep in a large email chain (e.g. message 3, 4, 5+ in the thread history) and they are no longer an active participant in the recent correspondence.
5. NESTED EMAIL ATTACHMENTS (RECURSIVE CARRIERS): If the top-level email is unrelated but contains an attached email (.eml/.msg file) that matches the KEEP criteria, you MUST mark both the attached email AND the parent carrier email as "keep".
   - Case Study: Anne sends an email to Bob. Anne's email contains an attached email from the Subject to Carlos.
   - Analysis: Keep the attached email because the Subject is a participant. Keep Anne's email because it is the physical carrier of the attachment and must be preserved to allow extraction.
6. OUTPUT FORMAT: You must return ONLY a raw JSON object. Do not wrap the output in markdown code blocks (```json). Do not add conversational text.
Format exactly like this: {"decision": "keep" | "discard", "reason": "Brief justification."}

Morning Anna,




Just following up on the below. With the good news that PG's application to resign as Lead Solicitor having been put on ice (pending further clarification from Pogust Goodhead or approval of the proposed agency relationship by the SRA), we need to consider
 the implications of this ruling. 




Notwithstanding the case leads concerns over the AA, given the firm's intention that this AA arrangement was to create a firebreak between the Case Leads and the potential of interference from Gramercy, that we remain as lead Solicitor, we consider that this
 creates arguably an even bigger need for there to be clear daylight between the case leads and such potential interference. If there is a fear of funder interference, then this is even more acute in circumstances where we hold the role of Lead Solicitor, as
 opposed to that of another Claimant Firm, not least (as we have said before) because we owe duties to all clients, not just those of PG. Can you please give us your / the board's opinion on next steps?




Pending the response to this, some of the below issues (re staff alienation etc) may become live again, especially the questions at the foot of the email - some of which require answers in any event. We  also need to know whether the firm is intending on providing
 the Court with further information (if so, it should be made clear that the Case Leads, while intent on finding a solution, had the AA executed over their heads) or whether they intend to seek SRA approval of the AA (again making clear the Case Leads concerns). 




We have also become aware of a letter from Slaughter and May regarding litigation conduct and that this may have in turn resulted in or precipitated resignations from others in the business. If there are such concerns that have been raised regarding litigation
 conduct in the firm, that we are all senior employees of, then we need to know and we need to know what the position of the firm is. In case it was not obvious, each of us are considering our own regulatory position and whether we need to self report to the
 SRA and having this information will assist us in assessing this.




Thanks,




Case Leads

Subject: Wish List & Requests
 






Hi Anna,




Following on from yesterday and the calls with LD, a few things we would suggest are raised with Martyn. Firstly, it is important to say the Case Leads and PG team are wildly committed to this trial. That should not be in question.
 However, the AA (the executed version of which the case leads were only sent at 9.22AM this morning), which has been referred to in Court documents and has been incepted without the consent of those persons it applies to (either expressly in the case of the
 Case Leads or, as far as the wider team is concerned, by implication), causes concern. Additionally, the case leads have also raised serious concerns about the staff's  mental health that are yet to be addressed by the firm.




The AA was incepted with little to no visibility or consideration for how it will practically work (as is clear given Martyn's explanation in ​the call on 8 October was substantially different to our understanding of what it means,
 a view which we consider you, also on that call, shared). We need further clarity on the AA. This is true for both for the Case Leads, and the PG staff who will be indirectly subject to it - by way of taking instructions from the Case Leads who are under the
 supervision of Leigh Day.  As we have already told you, there is a real risk of the substantive PG team being entirely alienated by this agreement. These concerns were evidently ignored (including our concerns over the mental health and well-being of the staff)
 given it was executed without further recourse to us.  It also remains unclear what, if any, interaction LD is to have with the wider PG team, if they are not subject to the AA (and therefore direction and supervision), and whether, given this, the PG team
 would need to revert to one of the Case Leads for every interaction, instruction, discussion had with the LD team. An obvious example of this is the trial bundle/logistics workstreams which have largely been left between the excellent PG associates and LD
 with limited input from the case leads. It is fair to say the PG team carries that workstream and LD are unprepared to take it on. Similarly with Opus and issues at this morning's hearing. 




It would be helpful for an explanation, and for the physical AA, to be sent out to the wider PG team along with some practical guidance about what it means. It would be inappropriate for the Case Leads to do this given: i) we
 haven’t agreed to the AA; and ii) it has been incepted against our consent.




It would be helpful if the explanation covered:





what LD expect from the PG team  - do they simply expect the PG teams to "do what they're told, when they're told", or is there still going to be a collaborative
 approach (the former seems more likely given how things have happened over the last few days); 


how the "do what they're told, when they're told" works - or, indeed wider interaction works, in circumstances where the team isn't caught by the agreement. Will they need to take each instruction and run it past a Case Lead?

what happens in circumstances where the PG teams disagree with LDs position on decisions? How does this get resolved between the firms? We stress this is not a hypothetical. Aside from wider case strategy
 we have had immediate differences in opinion last week in terms of costs, with decisions being made and taken without reference to PG. This impacts all claimants, and, of course PG's clients. Further, in terms of wider points, as we have pointed out, LD do
 not have clients on some of the secondary or ALGLO cases, all of which are bound by the PDD trial judgment. It is easy to anticipate a diversion of opinion/strategy as the PDD trial develops which could impact PG only cases/clients and for which, under the
 AA the Case Leads cannot wear two hats.  

how working practices are going to change, both outwardly to the Ds and Court etc, and whether a working group should be set up to standardise approach e.g. do all things on the PG SharePoint move across
 to LD - what is the timeframe, how is it co-ordinated? Whilst an administrative concern this does have significance in terms of sheer volume and also maintaining/transferring admin rights for links particularly where the Defendants and the Court already retain
 access. 

How does it work for the costs team? 





Each of these, along with sight of the AA, will go some way to helping the PG staff understand the agreement they are now working under and hopefully to stop the wheels from falling off. This will also assist in answering questions
 the Case Leads have, but it will not, we doubt, satisfy any regulatory concerns we have, and we request again the Board's complete answer to our note of 05.10.2025 (under cover of email of Sarah Bingham). To date we have not had any answer from you. 




On this point, we thought it helpful to also compile a few outstanding requests from our end to you / the Board. We should also say thank you again for speaking to Alicia and arranging the call with the employment solicitor. While
 we hope this will assist in clarifying the position in terms of whether this AA can be imposed upon us and not contravene our employment contracts, it will not be able to answer any of our regulatory concerns (in respect of the AA and wider regulatory concerns).
 These really can only be answered by the following: 





the advice from BWKC or any other counsel on the AA. This is especially true where many of the concerns we have raised overlap with those in the HSFK letter - including the regulatory position for us
 as lawyers, and the position on client consent. We still have not consented to the AA and we all have significant regulatory concerns. In particular we have not seen any advice which contradicts our position that client consent is necessary for the AA.

Re the AA and how strategic decisions are made, a very practical question: in circumstances where LD and PG (either collaboratively or by PG being informed)
 make a decision, do the PG bods have to in turn report these to the Board / AV? Do we have to report where decisions have been made that we do not agree with? What is our internal reporting matrix for issues such as this? 

Will our COLP, in their role as COLP, be giving us sign off on the agreement, in addition to the Counsel advice?

As our COLP is now also a case lead (for Pan NOx and it appears individual cases), is there a delineation of the COLP roles, from the role of case lead,
 and CEO of the firm? How is this safeguarded?





If these questions are not answered to a satisfactory standard, then our regulatory concerns will remain and as regulated persons, we will need to consider our positions and what, if any, further steps we need to take.




Thanks,




Case Leads

 I'm more than happy to do so. 


This email is in two parts: i) to address my notice period and when may be a good time for me to depart the firm;
 and ii) to address on-going travel and litigation needs with a view to finding a pragmatic way to handle future travel etc.


Notice Period


I agree that we need to work collaboratively to find an appropriate point for me to leave the firm, both to ensure
 the clients are protected and not disadvantaged, and to ensure that I am protected and not prejudiced. My current leave date is I understand the 15 December 2025. There are various important deadlines between now and then an to add a little more colour to
 those deadlines, the deadlines we have approaching (demarcated as PDD or Quantum) are as follows:



06.10.2025 – PTR 2 (PDD)
10.10.2025 – receipt of disclosure from Defendants (Quantum)
13.10.2025 – Trial starts (PDD)
21.11.2025 – Individual Particulars of Quantum to be filed and served (Quantum)
11.12.2025 – receipt of disclosure from Defendants (Quantum)
19.12.2025 – Trial ends (PDD)



19.12.2025 – Applications for January 2026 CMC (Quantum)




As is evident, the litigation has a large number of critical deadlines looming. Overlayed with this, is the added complication of each OEM having its own CRO, as well as an overall
 Pan-NOx CRO.


Each individual must apply to the Defendants (individually per CRO and to all Defendants for the Pan-Lead CRO) for
 permission to be entered into that CRO. This takes up to 5 working days. There is also a process for applying to be removed from each CRO which can, in itself, take some days.


Given the level of confidential information in the NOx litigations, someone who is not in one, or all, of the CROs,
 is necessarily extremely limited as to what they can see, do and work on. For example, they could not actively participate in the trial, nor could they provide any type of meaningful input into any of the directions that fall across the period that they are
 not in the CRO i.e. the IPQs. If therefore I am held to work my notice until 15 December, I will be unable to attend trial for the final week before Christmas, nor will I will be able to really assist with any work on quantum disclosure, or work on the applications
 / witness statements for the January 2026 CMC.


Considering this, we (both me and Pogust Goodhead) need to realistically consider when my departure should fall, as
 it should come at a time that will be at the least detriment of the claimants.


To that end, it seems sensible, and would be in everyone’s interests, for me to depart Pogust Goodhead on a date that
 will allow me to start my new role and be re-entered into the various CROs, which does not conflict with any of those deadlines, nor run over a critical part of the trial that I am intended to participate in. To require me to serve my notice such that I leave
 the firm on a date which conflicts with a major deadline would be of significant detriment to the clients, not only of this firm, but to other firms as well.


Having considered the timetable and what is genuinely in the best interests of everyone, especially the clients, it
 would appear the best date for me to depart Pogust Goodhead is the 17 October. This date falls after the opening submissions, and across the Normal Driving Conditions expert evidence (which is plainly of importance, but falls at the lower end of the scale
 of importance considering the other critical tasks over the trial period). Exiting Pogust Goodhead then, will allow me sufficient time to commence my new role before substantive evidence relating to the manufacturers starts.


Any other date past this, will cause significant issues with my involvement over key aspects of the trial and, I believe,
 will have a negative impact on the claimants. For a Partner with current conduct of an ALGLO, who has detailed knowledge of all of the cases across the Pan-NOx Litigation, to be unable to participate in the trial, is not in anyone’s interests. The obvious
 link is that any prohibition on me being able to work on these cases, also directly impacts the Pogust Goodhead claimants and the prospects of their claims being successfully concluded.


Without wishing this to become a confrontational or protracted process (as I am committed to progressing this in a
 professional and orderly fashion), if Pogust Goodhead wish me to remain in post past this date, I would ask that they provide good reason why, including an explanation of why they do not believe this will impact the clients (including why they believe it is
 in the clients best interests) including the trial timetable and the quantum deadlines.


I would ask this be provided to assist me with any future queries that may be raised of me in respect of compliance
 with my professional and regulatory obligations i.e. "why did you leave during the PDD Trial or  why didn't you leave at a point when you would be restricted from working on critical quantum workstreams?".


Future Travel


While we resolve the issue of my notice period, I am conscious that it is “business as usual” and I am committed to
 this. As such, I will be needing to continue to travel to London for work in the office and for attendance at trial (while I am still employed by the firm).


I appreciate the arrangement I have with the firm is that they will book my flights for me. Given I wish to make bookings
 into the future, past the date which I have given above as my preferred leave date, I would suggest that it is more pragmatic, to ensure they the firm is not put to more expense than is needed, for me to take charge of booking my flights, which I can then
 claim back through expenses. Going forward then, flights which occur over the dates of my employment, I would seek to recover in expenses. For any flights booked that occur past my leave date, I would then cover the cost of myself (as I would no longer be
 in the employ of the firm).


This strikes me as inherently more sensible than continuing to have the firm book my flights, as in an instance where
 the firm has booked a flight for me which is due to take off after my leave date, I would not be able to travel on that flight, and I would need to re-book the flight most likely at a higher price.


Additional to this (and at a higher cost), is the flat that the firm has rented for me the duration of the trial.
 This rental starts on 6 October and runs until 21 December. I am intending on using this for as long as I am with the firm. The firm however, especially if they are agreeable to my suggested leave date, may wish to consider cancelling this booking and instead
 booking me into hotels until my leave date. This may be something that the firm considered a more pragmatic and financially sound option. I am comfortable either way and am happy to have an open dialogue on how best to manage this.


Until hearing otherwise, I will change my flight booking system such that I will make flight bookings personally and
 the recover the cost via expenses, and I will proceed as if to stay in that flat over the remainder of my employment.

Michael

 else at the last minute; andGiven the trial starts in October with summer in between, I anticipate at least some of the trial prep costs will be incurred before the end of July. I expect some tranches of
 brief will be incurred, and there will also be at least some solicitor work (eg I can see there are trial bundle deadlines in July at [52]-[55]).

 end of July 2026. I’m in PG/LDs hands on that. If that’s something we can say, then yes, I can see the argument that there is unlikely to be a set of circumstances which lead to needing cover for the ‘full’ T3 period. If it is more complicated that that, T3

Thanks
Simon"}

 policies.


Following the handing down of the judgment (10th September 2025) after the Second Costs Management Hearing (15-16 July 2025), the Defendants have revisited their
 position on applications for security for costs. We have therefore undertaken a further review of the potential adverse costs resulting from the Tranche 3 Quantum Trial and the Second General Budget. 


Previously, our assessment of ATE sufficiency was calculated on the following basis:



60% of the Defendants’ claimed incurred costs;



60% of the Defendants’ claimed budgeted costs; and



100% of approved future costs to Spring 2026.

50% of the Defendants’ claimed incurred costs;



50% of the Defendants’ claimed budgeted costs; and



100% of approved future costs to 31 July 2026.
